compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
All six rows use the same information, responsibilities, deadline, and decision authority. Either person can use either approach.

| Same task, information, and authority | INTP: possible emphasis | ISTJ: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reviewing the same brief and past examples | Look for recurring connections that suggest possible approaches | Check what the brief and past examples document about steps and outcomes | S/N: possible patterns and documented details |
| Agreeing on a response to the same instruction | Keep multiple workable arrangements open until the same details are confirmed | Set a provisional schedule and assign responsibility within the same limits | J/P: open options and provisional outward structure |
| Reviewing the same batch of documents | Notice patterns and relationships across the same cases | Check the specific dates, descriptions, and findings in the same records | S/N: connections across records and concrete details |
| Updating the same plan after a requirements change | Keep feasible revisions open until the effects of the change are confirmed | Agree on a provisional revision schedule subject to the same constraints | J/P: retaining options and setting a provisional arrangement |
| Reviewing the same report of a problem | What recurring pattern might explain the issue across similar cases? | Which steps and observations does the report actually record? | S/N: possible patterns and specific facts. Both can inform the review. |
| Scheduling a review of the same proposed change to a rule | Keep several feasible review dates open while checking availability | Set a provisional review date within the same requirements | J/P: keeping options open or forming an outward arrangement |

An auditor may know which records to use. A researcher may look for a pattern worth testing. Training, time, and responsibility can explain either approach. The table cannot establish type or ability.
compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Either person might check figures and revise wording because the task requires it. Carefulness and the amount of time spent on a review cannot establish type.

Shared I concerns where attention and energy tend to go. Shared T concerns the criteria used in decisions. Neither identifies someone’s speaking habits or intellectual ability.

S/N asks what information a person gives weight to. J/P asks how they handle outward commitments and open options. Someone can rely on verified precedents while keeping a plan open, or explore new possibilities while committing to a provisional schedule.

Asking whether a procedure was followed and asking whether it still serves its purpose are useful checks. Either person can ask both.

### INTP and ISTJ: the same deliverable, coherent or handoverable

In a fictional handover, two reviewers receive the same document, deadline, and authority. Both can check for unsupported assumptions and verify that the successor has the steps and contacts needed to do the work.

Which issue needs attention depends on the work. An unfamiliar successor may need clearer instructions. A recurring exception may require an explanation of why a step exists.

A clear explanation can still lack usable steps. A complete checklist can still carry forward a bad assumption. A handover can address both.

One draft may need a note about an inconsistency and another about an unassigned step. Who notices either issue can reflect expertise and assigned responsibilities.

### INTP and ISTJ: why the perceiving pair is shared and the judging pair changes

Both types are introverted, so the outward-facing process is auxiliary. INTP’s P points to auxiliary extraverted Intuition (Ne), which supports dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). ISTJ’s J points to auxiliary extraverted Thinking (Te), which supports dominant introverted Sensing (Si).

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. Ne is auxiliary for INTP and inferior for ISTJ. Si is dominant for ISTJ and tertiary for INTP in this convention.

The judging processes occupy different positions and face different directions: INTP has dominant Ti and inferior Fe, while ISTJ has auxiliary Te and tertiary Fi in this notation. Neither the shared nor the different processes can tell you whether two people will agree on the facts.

The Foundation lists tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si) and tertiary Feeling for ISTJ (Fe or Fi). This page uses Si and Fi. The alternatives leave the first two positions unchanged. See the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) and [ISTJ profile](/en/personality/istj).
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
Both examples are fictional. They illustrate how people use the same information and coordinate a handover. Handover quality depends on what the recipient needs to do, what is documented, and what support is available.

### INTP and ISTJ: a leaving-the-job handover list

In this fictional departure, two people have the same records and deadline. The work includes recurring reports, supplier reconciliation, a migration in progress, and issues whose history needs explaining.

One way to organize the material is by task, owner, due date, and contact. Another is by dependencies and assumptions, such as why two reports use different definitions. Either person can use both structures.

A checklist can leave an exception unexplained. A background note can leave the recipient unsure where to start. Use both to check what the successor needs.

Review a routine task and a representative exception with the successor under the same conditions. If they get stuck, distinguish missing information from missing access or training. A page count cannot establish whether the handover works.

Record who can complete each task, what remains unresolved, and who will follow up. A gap is a question to investigate, not an indicator of personality.

### INTP and ISTJ: a friend goes abroad for two years and leaves a cat

In this fictional example, a friend asks two people to care for their cat. Both receive the same care notes and contact details. They can check which routines are confirmed and what arrangements remain open.

The handover can distinguish the owner’s routine instructions from questions for the veterinarian. Either person can make sure both sets of information are accessible.

For concerns about the animal’s health, contact a veterinarian and follow their guidance. The fictional handover illustrates how people organize information without deciding what a symptom means.

compare_blocks.body:
Either person may revise wording because a statement is unclear or the records do not match. Editing one sentence cannot establish type.

An occupation can teach particular routines and vocabulary. It cannot identify a person’s preferences or establish who is suited to a job.

An INTP can write a usable process and an ISTJ can question an assumption. Either skill can come from practice. It does not establish S/N or J/P.

In this notation, both types have Si and Ne in different positions. Neither that overlap nor the shared T predicts whether two people will agree.

comparison.summary:
INTP and ISTJ share Introversion (I) and Thinking (T). They differ on Sensing/Intuition and Judging/Perceiving. Those two pairs concern information and outward arrangements, respectively.

- **I (shared):** Introversion describes attention and energy directed more toward inner ideas and reflection. It does not determine how much someone speaks.
- **T (shared):** Thinking emphasizes principles and consistently applied criteria. Both types can also consider how a decision affects people.
- **S/N:** ISTJ’s Sensing emphasizes observable details and relevant experience. INTP’s Intuition emphasizes connections, patterns, and possibilities.
- **J/P:** ISTJ’s Judging favors structure and closure in dealings with the outside world. INTP’s Perceiving favors keeping options open to new information. Either person can make or revise a plan.

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. Ne is auxiliary for INTP and inferior for ISTJ. This notation shows Si as tertiary for INTP and dominant for ISTJ. The judging processes differ: Ti and Fe for INTP, Te and Fi for ISTJ.

The Foundation gives alternatives for the tertiary attitudes. These positions describe preferences within the model and cannot establish what a person does first or how well they work.

compare_blocks.body:
INTP and ISTJ share Introversion (I) and Thinking (T). They differ on Sensing/Intuition and Judging/Perceiving. Those two pairs concern information and outward arrangements, respectively.

- **I (shared):** Introversion describes attention and energy directed more toward inner ideas and reflection. It does not determine how much someone speaks.
- **T (shared):** Thinking emphasizes principles and consistently applied criteria. Both types can also consider how a decision affects people.
- **S/N:** ISTJ’s Sensing emphasizes observable details and relevant experience. INTP’s Intuition emphasizes connections, patterns, and possibilities.
- **J/P:** ISTJ’s Judging favors structure and closure in dealings with the outside world. INTP’s Perceiving favors keeping options open to new information. Either person can make or revise a plan.

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. Ne is auxiliary for INTP and inferior for ISTJ. This notation shows Si as tertiary for INTP and dominant for ISTJ. The judging processes differ: Ti and Fe for INTP, Te and Fi for ISTJ.

The Foundation gives alternatives for the tertiary attitudes. These positions describe preferences within the model and cannot establish what a person does first or how well they work.
compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
All six rows use the same information, responsibilities, deadline, and decision authority. Either person can use either approach.

| Same task, information, and authority | INTP: possible emphasis | ISTJ: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reviewing the same brief and past examples | Look for recurring connections that suggest possible approaches | Check what the brief and past examples document about steps and outcomes | S/N: possible patterns and documented details |
| Agreeing on a response to the same instruction | Keep multiple workable arrangements open until the same details are confirmed | Set a provisional schedule and assign responsibility within the same limits | J/P: open options and provisional outward structure |
| Reviewing the same batch of documents | Notice patterns and relationships across the same cases | Check the specific dates, descriptions, and findings in the same records | S/N: connections across records and concrete details |
| Updating the same plan after a requirements change | Keep feasible revisions open until the effects of the change are confirmed | Agree on a provisional revision schedule subject to the same constraints | J/P: retaining options and setting a provisional arrangement |
| Reviewing the same report of a problem | What recurring pattern might explain the issue across similar cases? | Which steps and observations does the report actually record? | S/N: possible patterns and specific facts. Both can inform the review. |
| Scheduling a review of the same proposed change to a rule | Keep several feasible review dates open while checking availability | Set a provisional review date within the same requirements | J/P: keeping options open or forming an outward arrangement |

An auditor may know which records to use. A researcher may look for a pattern worth testing. Training, time, and responsibility can explain either approach. The table cannot establish type or ability.
compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Either person might check figures and revise wording because the task requires it. Carefulness and the amount of time spent on a review cannot establish type.

Shared I concerns where attention and energy tend to go. Shared T concerns the criteria used in decisions. Neither identifies someone’s speaking habits or intellectual ability.

S/N asks what information a person gives weight to. J/P asks how they handle outward commitments and open options. Someone can rely on verified precedents while keeping a plan open, or explore new possibilities while committing to a provisional schedule.

Asking whether a procedure was followed and asking whether it still serves its purpose are useful checks. Either person can ask both.

### INTP and ISTJ: the same deliverable, coherent or handoverable

In a fictional handover, two reviewers receive the same document, deadline, and authority. Both can check for unsupported assumptions and verify that the successor has the steps and contacts needed to do the work.

Which issue needs attention depends on the work. An unfamiliar successor may need clearer instructions. A recurring exception may require an explanation of why a step exists.

A clear explanation can still lack usable steps. A complete checklist can still carry forward a bad assumption. A handover can address both.

One draft may need a note about an inconsistency and another about an unassigned step. Who notices either issue can reflect expertise and assigned responsibilities.

### INTP and ISTJ: why the perceiving pair is shared and the judging pair changes

Both types are introverted, so the outward-facing process is auxiliary. INTP’s P points to auxiliary extraverted Intuition (Ne), which supports dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). ISTJ’s J points to auxiliary extraverted Thinking (Te), which supports dominant introverted Sensing (Si).

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. Ne is auxiliary for INTP and inferior for ISTJ. Si is dominant for ISTJ and tertiary for INTP in this convention.

The judging processes occupy different positions and face different directions: INTP has dominant Ti and inferior Fe, while ISTJ has auxiliary Te and tertiary Fi in this notation. Neither the shared nor the different processes can tell you whether two people will agree on the facts.

The Foundation lists tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si) and tertiary Feeling for ISTJ (Fe or Fi). This page uses Si and Fi. The alternatives leave the first two positions unchanged. See the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) and [ISTJ profile](/en/personality/istj).
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
Both examples are fictional. They illustrate how people use the same information and coordinate a handover. Handover quality depends on what the recipient needs to do, what is documented, and what support is available.

### INTP and ISTJ: a leaving-the-job handover list

In this fictional departure, two people have the same records and deadline. The work includes recurring reports, supplier reconciliation, a migration in progress, and issues whose history needs explaining.

One way to organize the material is by task, owner, due date, and contact. Another is by dependencies and assumptions, such as why two reports use different definitions. Either person can use both structures.

A checklist can leave an exception unexplained. A background note can leave the recipient unsure where to start. Use both to check what the successor needs.

Review a routine task and a representative exception with the successor under the same conditions. If they get stuck, distinguish missing information from missing access or training. A page count cannot establish whether the handover works.

Record who can complete each task, what remains unresolved, and who will follow up. A gap is a question to investigate, not an indicator of personality.

### INTP and ISTJ: a friend goes abroad for two years and leaves a cat

In this fictional example, a friend asks two people to care for their cat. Both receive the same care notes and contact details. They can check which routines are confirmed and what arrangements remain open.

The handover can distinguish the owner’s routine instructions from questions for the veterinarian. Either person can make sure both sets of information are accessible.

For concerns about the animal’s health, contact a veterinarian and follow their guidance. The fictional handover illustrates how people organize information without deciding what a symptom means.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
Either person may revise wording because a statement is unclear or the records do not match. Editing one sentence cannot establish type.

An occupation can teach particular routines and vocabulary. It cannot identify a person’s preferences or establish who is suited to a job.

An INTP can write a usable process and an ISTJ can question an assumption. Either skill can come from practice. It does not establish S/N or J/P.

In this notation, both types have Si and Ne in different positions. Neither that overlap nor the shared T predicts whether two people will agree.

faq_blocks.answer:
Both types prefer Thinking in the model and can use the same decision criteria. Which standards apply can follow from the task, risk, and responsibilities.

An ISTJ can propose changing a rule when a case exposes a weakness. An INTP can follow the same rule when it meets the requirements. Those actions do not by themselves identify either preference.
faq_blocks.question: Do the two hold the same standard?

faq_blocks.answer:
In this notation, Ne is auxiliary for INTP and inferior for ISTJ. Si is dominant for ISTJ and tertiary for INTP.

The placements describe roles within type dynamics. The Foundation offers alternatives for the tertiary attitude, which can change the exact overlap. Either person can check a precedent or explore an alternative.
faq_blocks.question: Both share Ne and Si — what does the difference in seat mean?

faq_blocks.answer:
Yes. Either type can revise a process or document it carefully.

A failed process and a handover requirement can explain those choices. Neither filling in a form nor changing a procedure establishes S/N or J/P.
faq_blocks.question: ISTJ also tears up a process and redoes it, INTP also fills in a form meticulously — counterexamples?

faq_blocks.answer:
Either person may leave out information a successor needs. Compare the handover to the actual responsibilities and information available.

Check whether the successor understands why each step exists, knows where to start, and has the necessary access and training. Each gap requires a different fix.
faq_blocks.question: In a handover, what might each of them miss?

faq_blocks.answer:
A team may disagree on whether to release a provisional draft or keep options open for another round of review. Either person can take either view.

Agree which points are still open, what new evidence would change the draft, and when it needs a decision. Follow the agreed review deadline.
faq_blocks.question: Working together, what kind of disagreement shows up at the final draft?

faq_blocks.answer:
Start by checking whether the two results came from comparable assessments.

Compare the instrument, version, language, and scoring guidance. If comparable reports give interpretable S/N and J/P scores, use the instrument’s guidance for each. Consider what situations you had in mind. A change in labels alone cannot establish why the result changed.

jsonld.name: INTP vs ISTJ: S/N, J/P, and Cognitive Functions

sections.body_md:
INTP and ISTJ share Introversion (I) and Thinking (T). They differ on Sensing/Intuition and Judging/Perceiving. Those two pairs concern information and outward arrangements, respectively.

- **I (shared):** Introversion describes attention and energy directed more toward inner ideas and reflection. It does not determine how much someone speaks.
- **T (shared):** Thinking emphasizes principles and consistently applied criteria. Both types can also consider how a decision affects people.
- **S/N:** ISTJ’s Sensing emphasizes observable details and relevant experience. INTP’s Intuition emphasizes connections, patterns, and possibilities.
- **J/P:** ISTJ’s Judging favors structure and closure in dealings with the outside world. INTP’s Perceiving favors keeping options open to new information. Either person can make or revise a plan.

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. Ne is auxiliary for INTP and inferior for ISTJ. This notation shows Si as tertiary for INTP and dominant for ISTJ. The judging processes differ: Ti and Fe for INTP, Te and Fi for ISTJ.

The Foundation gives alternatives for the tertiary attitudes. These positions describe preferences within the model and cannot establish what a person does first or how well they work.
sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
Either person might check figures and revise wording because the task requires it. Carefulness and the amount of time spent on a review cannot establish type.

Shared I concerns where attention and energy tend to go. Shared T concerns the criteria used in decisions. Neither identifies someone’s speaking habits or intellectual ability.

S/N asks what information a person gives weight to. J/P asks how they handle outward commitments and open options. Someone can rely on verified precedents while keeping a plan open, or explore new possibilities while committing to a provisional schedule.

Asking whether a procedure was followed and asking whether it still serves its purpose are useful checks. Either person can ask both.

### INTP and ISTJ: the same deliverable, coherent or handoverable

In a fictional handover, two reviewers receive the same document, deadline, and authority. Both can check for unsupported assumptions and verify that the successor has the steps and contacts needed to do the work.

Which issue needs attention depends on the work. An unfamiliar successor may need clearer instructions. A recurring exception may require an explanation of why a step exists.

A clear explanation can still lack usable steps. A complete checklist can still carry forward a bad assumption. A handover can address both.

One draft may need a note about an inconsistency and another about an unassigned step. Who notices either issue can reflect expertise and assigned responsibilities.

### INTP and ISTJ: why the perceiving pair is shared and the judging pair changes

Both types are introverted, so the outward-facing process is auxiliary. INTP’s P points to auxiliary extraverted Intuition (Ne), which supports dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). ISTJ’s J points to auxiliary extraverted Thinking (Te), which supports dominant introverted Sensing (Si).

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. Ne is auxiliary for INTP and inferior for ISTJ. Si is dominant for ISTJ and tertiary for INTP in this convention.

The judging processes occupy different positions and face different directions: INTP has dominant Ti and inferior Fe, while ISTJ has auxiliary Te and tertiary Fi in this notation. Neither the shared nor the different processes can tell you whether two people will agree on the facts.

The Foundation lists tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si) and tertiary Feeling for ISTJ (Fe or Fi). This page uses Si and Fi. The alternatives leave the first two positions unchanged. See the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) and [ISTJ profile](/en/personality/istj).
sections.title: INTP and ISTJ: what they share, and where the two axes differ

sections.body_md:
All six rows use the same information, responsibilities, deadline, and decision authority. Either person can use either approach.

| Same task, information, and authority | INTP: possible emphasis | ISTJ: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reviewing the same brief and past examples | Look for recurring connections that suggest possible approaches | Check what the brief and past examples document about steps and outcomes | S/N: possible patterns and documented details |
| Agreeing on a response to the same instruction | Keep multiple workable arrangements open until the same details are confirmed | Set a provisional schedule and assign responsibility within the same limits | J/P: open options and provisional outward structure |
| Reviewing the same batch of documents | Notice patterns and relationships across the same cases | Check the specific dates, descriptions, and findings in the same records | S/N: connections across records and concrete details |
| Updating the same plan after a requirements change | Keep feasible revisions open until the effects of the change are confirmed | Agree on a provisional revision schedule subject to the same constraints | J/P: retaining options and setting a provisional arrangement |
| Reviewing the same report of a problem | What recurring pattern might explain the issue across similar cases? | Which steps and observations does the report actually record? | S/N: possible patterns and specific facts. Both can inform the review. |
| Scheduling a review of the same proposed change to a rule | Keep several feasible review dates open while checking availability | Set a provisional review date within the same requirements | J/P: keeping options open or forming an outward arrangement |

An auditor may know which records to use. A researcher may look for a pattern worth testing. Training, time, and responsibility can explain either approach. The table cannot establish type or ability.
sections.title: INTP and ISTJ in one minute

sections.body_md:
Both examples are fictional. They illustrate how people use the same information and coordinate a handover. Handover quality depends on what the recipient needs to do, what is documented, and what support is available.

### INTP and ISTJ: a leaving-the-job handover list

In this fictional departure, two people have the same records and deadline. The work includes recurring reports, supplier reconciliation, a migration in progress, and issues whose history needs explaining.

One way to organize the material is by task, owner, due date, and contact. Another is by dependencies and assumptions, such as why two reports use different definitions. Either person can use both structures.

A checklist can leave an exception unexplained. A background note can leave the recipient unsure where to start. Use both to check what the successor needs.

Review a routine task and a representative exception with the successor under the same conditions. If they get stuck, distinguish missing information from missing access or training. A page count cannot establish whether the handover works.

Record who can complete each task, what remains unresolved, and who will follow up. A gap is a question to investigate, not an indicator of personality.

### INTP and ISTJ: a friend goes abroad for two years and leaves a cat

In this fictional example, a friend asks two people to care for their cat. Both receive the same care notes and contact details. They can check which routines are confirmed and what arrangements remain open.

The handover can distinguish the owner’s routine instructions from questions for the veterinarian. Either person can make sure both sets of information are accessible.

For concerns about the animal’s health, contact a veterinarian and follow their guidance. The fictional handover illustrates how people organize information without deciding what a symptom means.
sections.title: INTP and ISTJ in two fictional scenarios

sections.body_md:
Either person may revise wording because a statement is unclear or the records do not match. Editing one sentence cannot establish type.

An occupation can teach particular routines and vocabulary. It cannot identify a person’s preferences or establish who is suited to a job.

An INTP can write a usable process and an ISTJ can question an assumption. Either skill can come from practice. It does not establish S/N or J/P.

In this notation, both types have Si and Ne in different positions. Neither that overlap nor the shared T predicts whether two people will agree.
sections.title: INTP and ISTJ: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
Compare the assessment, version, language, and scoring guidance. Consider whether your answers drew on what you normally prefer or what a specific job requires.

If comparable reports give interpretable S/N and J/P scores, review each against the tool’s guidance. A letter change alone cannot establish which score was near a cutoff or why it changed.

Recall several comparable decisions where you had room to choose. Write down the concrete information you used, the patterns or possibilities you considered, and what you committed to or left open. Use the notes for reflection. They do not produce a score or determine type.
sections.title: INTP and ISTJ: how to keep observing

items.answer:
Both types prefer Thinking in the model and can use the same decision criteria. Which standards apply can follow from the task, risk, and responsibilities.

An ISTJ can propose changing a rule when a case exposes a weakness. An INTP can follow the same rule when it meets the requirements. Those actions do not by themselves identify either preference.
items.question: Do the two hold the same standard?

items.answer:
In this notation, Ne is auxiliary for INTP and inferior for ISTJ. Si is dominant for ISTJ and tertiary for INTP.

The placements describe roles within type dynamics. The Foundation offers alternatives for the tertiary attitude, which can change the exact overlap. Either person can check a precedent or explore an alternative.
items.question: Both share Ne and Si — what does the difference in seat mean?

items.answer:
Yes. Either type can revise a process or document it carefully.

A failed process and a handover requirement can explain those choices. Neither filling in a form nor changing a procedure establishes S/N or J/P.
items.question: ISTJ also tears up a process and redoes it, INTP also fills in a form meticulously — counterexamples?

items.answer:
Either person may leave out information a successor needs. Compare the handover to the actual responsibilities and information available.

Check whether the successor understands why each step exists, knows where to start, and has the necessary access and training. Each gap requires a different fix.
items.question: In a handover, what might each of them miss?

items.answer:
A team may disagree on whether to release a provisional draft or keep options open for another round of review. Either person can take either view.

Agree which points are still open, what new evidence would change the draft, and when it needs a decision. Follow the agreed review deadline.
items.question: Working together, what kind of disagreement shows up at the final draft?

items.answer:
Start by checking whether the two results came from comparable assessments.

Compare the instrument, version, language, and scoring guidance. If comparable reports give interpretable S/N and J/P scores, use the instrument’s guidance for each. Consider what situations you had in mind. A change in labels alone cannot establish why the result changed.

**Framework sources**: the definitions of the preferences follow the [Myers-Briggs official facts page](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts); the type-dynamics framework follows the [Foundation's note on type dynamics](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) and the [type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

**Function notation:** This page uses Ti–Ne–Si–Fe for INTP and Si–Te–Fi–Ne for ISTJ. The Foundation gives alternatives for tertiary attitudes. The dominant and auxiliary positions remain the same.

**Fictional examples:** The work handover and cat-care handover illustrate ways to organize the same information. They cannot establish type or substitute for veterinary advice.

**Scope limits**: the comparisons in the body describe emphasis inside a model and are not for ranking ability, hiring screens or predicting relationships; clinical judgements belong with qualified professionals.
